title: Twice as much enzyme
hook: Move substrate and watch a model rate grow.

knows: Enzymes catalyse reactions and substrate concentration can affect the rate.
doesNotKnow: At S = 2, B's rate is 16 × 2/(2 + 2) = 8; A's rate is 4. This model holds other conditions fixed.

misconception: A rate is always proportional to substrate at every concentration.
objective: Interpret a stated ideal enzyme-rate model at a fixed substrate level.

claims.text: Question, chart and reveal: In this ideal model, doubling active enzyme doubles Vmax from 8 in A to 16 in B while Km stays at 2. At S = 2, what is B's rate? At S = 2, B's rate is 16 × 2/(2 + 2) = 8; A's rate is 4. This model holds other conditions fixed.
claims.source: Substitute the stated parameters into v = Vmax S/(Km + S); enzyme context: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/6-5-enzymes

claims.text: The chart is an idealized model in arbitrary units, not a fitted measurement or universal law for every enzyme.
Recall: In the ideal model v = Vmax·S/(Km + S), what is v when S = Km? Substituting S = Km gives v = Vmax × Km/(2 Km) = Vmax/2.

recall.question: In the ideal model v = Vmax·S/(Km + S), what is v when S = Km?
recall.why: Substituting S = Km gives v = Vmax × Km/(2 Km) = Vmax/2.
